prompts: After seven days, independently explain: Represent a multiplication as equal groups, an array and repeated addition, and explain why they show the same product.
Apply the idea to a new context and justify the evidence or calculations used. This is a request for a governed retention task, not a scheduled or scored item.

pedagogy.rationale: Generate representations and worked reasoning from a versioned subject plan, then fade support before independent work and transfer.

prerequisiteAssumptions: Can read or access the text equivalent and explain a response in writing or speech.

misconceptions.description: Omits cross-products or loses the place value of a tens multiplier.
misconceptions.response: Split both factors into tens and ones; count all four rectangles and preserve the tens row value.

scenes.title: Split both dimensions
scenes.learnerAction: Use the model, complete its task, and explain what the representation shows.

content.body: Synthetic supply model. Seven equal groups of four contain 28 items: 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 28. The group count, row count and repeated-addition count agree. For larger products, a 24 by 13 rectangle splits at 20 + 4 and 10 + 3. Each unit square represents one item. Count all four smaller rectangles, not only two opposite corners.

accessibility.textAlternative: Synthetic supply model. Seven equal groups of four contain 28 items: 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 = 28. The group count, row count and repeated-addition count agree. For larger products, a 24 by 13 rectangle splits at 20 + 4 and 10 + 3. Each unit square represents one item. Count all four smaller rectangles, not only two opposite corners. 7 rows of 4 dots: 7 × 4 = 28. Seven groups of four and seven rows of four count the same 28 items. Trace the four partial rectangles and describe their dimensions. Find 24 × 13 by splitting it into parts.

blocks.caption: Seven groups of four and seven rows of four count the same 28 items.

blocks.prompt: Trace the four partial rectangles and describe their dimensions.

scenes.title: Four partial products
scenes.learnerAction: Use the model, complete its task, and explain what the representation shows.

content.body: The distributive property counts every non-overlapping part. The compact algorithm groups the same four parts into 24 x 3 and 24 x 10. The second row is tens; it represents 240, not 24.

accessibility.textAlternative: The distributive property counts every non-overlapping part. The compact algorithm groups the same four parts into 24 x 3 and 24 x 10. The second row is tens; it represents 240, not 24. 24 x 13 Step 1: Split both factors. (20 + 4)(10 + 3) Step 2: Calculate every rectangle. 200 + 60 + 40 + 12 = 312 Step 3: Regroup as algorithm rows. 24 × 3 + 24 × 10 = 72 + 240 = 312

scenes.title: Fill the four rectangles
scenes.learnerAction: Use the model, complete its task, and explain what the representation shows.

content.body: Split each factor into tens and ones. Complete the area model before entering a total; use the labels to explain your partial products.

accessibility.textAlternative: Split each factor into tens and ones. Complete the area model before entering a total; use the labels to explain your partial products. Which sum represents seven groups of four? Options: 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4 + 4; 7 + 4. Fill all four partial products, then add them. Find 23 × 14 by splitting it into parts. Calculate 23 times 14. Explain how every partial rectangle is counted. Total: write your answer. Calculate 16 times 12. Explain how every partial rectangle is counted. Total: write your answer.

items.prompt: Which sum represents seven groups of four?

options.feedback: Seven equal addends of four count 28 items.
Adding the group count and group size does not count the items in every group.

blocks.prompt: Fill all four partial products, then add them.
Calculate 23 times 14. Explain how every partial rectangle is counted.

misconceptions.feedback: You counted only tens-times-tens and ones-times-ones. Include 20 times 4 and 3 times 10 too.
The 1 tens in 14 means 10, not 1. Preserve place value in the tens partial product.

hints: Multiply each part of one factor by each part of the other, then add four products.
afterAttempt: Each partial rectangle occurs once, with no gap or overlap.

The 1 tens in 12 means 10, not 1. Preserve place value in the tens partial product.

hints: Multiply each part of one factor by each part of the other, then add four products.

scenes.title: Multiply two-digit numbers independently
scenes.learnerAction: Use the model, complete its task, and explain what the representation shows.

content.body: Choose an area model, partial products or the compact algorithm. Show your method on paper, then enter the total. Explain why the tens row has its place value.

accessibility.textAlternative: Choose an area model, partial products or the compact algorithm. Show your method on paper, then enter the total. Explain why the tens row has its place value. Which multiplication and sum represent six rows of five? Options: 6 x 5 = 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 + 5 = 30; 6 + 5 = 11. Calculate 32 times 24. Explain how every partial rectangle is counted. Total: write your answer. Calculate 17 times 18. Explain how every partial rectangle is counted. Total: write your answer.

scenes.title: Plan meeting seats
scenes.learnerAction: How many audience chairs remain after reserving 12? Explain the order of operations and check with an estimate.

content.body: Synthetic meeting plan. There are 18 rows with 14 chairs in each row. Reserve 12 chairs for presenters. Find the total and then the number available for the audience. Check whether your answer fits an estimate of 20 rows with 14 chairs.
